text:
Asha Patel: Quick profiler dump from last night's sm92 rollout — seeing ~18% token throughput drop on mixed-farm after driver bump to 545. Traces point to kernel-path thrash around seqlen 64-128; KV-cache churn spikes when we flip to the large-seqlen kernels.

Ravi Menon: Oof. Can you paste the perf counters and cap-detect output?

Asha Patel: Paste below — this is the region around the regression: 

```
perf: tokens/s  = 128k -> 105k
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.72 -> 0.54 (spike coincident with path switch)
kernel: picked=fast_path_seq32 on many GPUs, then fallback=matmul_seq128 on some tasks
driver: nvidia 545.23 -> heuristic shows different kernel_name hash
nvml: pci_id map returns 86/92 mixed on same host
```

Noah Kim: Two quick notes — 1) we've seen driver >540 remap some PCI IDs which trips our simple SM table. 2) our cap-probe currently prefers a single quick check (nvml pci id) instead of cuda device attributes; that gives false negatives for tensor cores/BF16 on some VMs.

Elena García: Also the batching heuristic: we switch kernel path when rolling_avg_seqlen > 48 for 3 consecutive batches. Bursty clients with a few seq128s flip it back and forth, which is exactly when KV cache miss rate spikes. Suggest adding hysteresis + cooldown and a min sample window.

Ravi Menon: Agreed. Proposed changes: 
- change cap-probe order: cudaGetDeviceAttribute(COMPUTE_CAPABILITY) -> cuDeviceGetAttribute for tensor core flags -> fallback to pci_id map
- add a capability flag: "tensor_core_aggressive" only if bf16 ops validated by microbench
- batching: require 20% sustained higher-seq share over 60s before flipping; add 10s cooldown.

Asha Patel: Microbench to validate BF16 path: I ran a small matmul microbench on the contested nodes: 
```
# quick run
./bench_matrix --dtype bf16 --size 2048
result: bf16_mflops ~ 0.92 * fp32_mflops on some cards -> borderline; fallback recommended unless driver reports tc fully working
```

Noah Kim: That explains it. If BF16 microbench < 0.95 we should avoid the bf16-optimized kernels by default. We can keep an opt-in flag per-cluster.

Elena García: For KV-cache: add an eviction smoothing metric. If eviction rate > 0.05 for >30s, avoid switching kernels for 60s. That should reduce thrash.

Asha Patel: I'll prototype the probe re-order + hysteresis in a branch. Plan: run canary on one pool for 24h.

infra-bot: Canary job created: canary/sm-hybrid-detect-2026-03-17 on pool gpu-p4x2 (id: cny-492)

Ravi Menon: Nice. Also add a tracing hook so we can correlate kernel pick events with kv-cache evictions (trace id -> kv event).

Asha Patel: Will do. Timeline: prototype today, internal bench tomorrow, canary by EOD.

deploy-bot: Rolling canary will block automated scale-up if kernel mismatch rate > 5% for 30m.

Noah Kim: Postmortem note — if this fixes perf, we should add an automated cap-detect regression test to CI that simulates mixed driver/pci_id combos.

Elena García: +1. Also document the new capability flag semantics and add a short troubleshooting blurb for SREs about driver-induced pci_id remapping.

Asha Patel: Created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4821 — prototype branch: feat/sm-hybrid-probe-kv-hysteresis

Ravi Menon: Thanks all. If the canary shows improvement, schedule a slow rollout and notify support docs. :thumbsup:

Noah Kim: I'll watch perf graphs and dump a second profiler after 6h.

Asha Patel: Thanks — ping me if you see any anomaly.
